sentences.text: Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the present applicant met the prosecutrix through Facebook, Instagram since 2021 and later, both have chatted in Whatsapp and had friendship between them.
On 24.12.2022, applicant came to see the prosecutrix and stayed with her till 27.12.2022 during that period the applicant committed Sexual intercourse.

Both of them were ready to marry but as per the allegation, the applicant has asked for obscene video which was sent by the prosecutrix but the said video got viral by the applicant in Whatsapp group upon which the prosecutrix has lodged the FIR against the applicant.
3.
It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
He submits that in this case, at the time of incident, the prosecutrix was a major girl.

He also submits that the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. has stated that they both were having friendship for last three to four years and they were connected through Facebook, Instagram and Whats-app (social media apps) and they have also made physical relationship but when she refused to marry the applicant he made the obscene video viral.

He lastly submits that the applicant is in jail since 23.03.2023 hence, he prays that the applicant be enlarged on bail.
Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:21285 4.

On the other hand, learned State counsel, opposed the bail application and submits that the present applicant has committed sexual intercourse with the victim and demanded her obscene video and then made it viral, therefore, he may not be released on bail, however, he fairly submits that applicant has no criminal antecedent.
5.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, particularly, the fact that at the time of incident the victim was a major lady and were in contact through social media for last three to four years as it is apparent from her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and there is Ishwar Banjare @ Kushuva vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106608545/

Bhatapara, District- Balodabazar (C.G.), for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 67 and 67A of the I.T. Act, be released on bail on him furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:21285 following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that they shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through their counsel.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against them under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuse the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicants are deliberate Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:21285 or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against them in accordance with law.

8. However, this Court hopes and trusts that the trial Court shall make earnest endeavour to conclude the trial within a period of eight months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order, if there is no legal impediment.
9. Office is directed to send a certified copy of this order to the trial Court concerned for necessary information and compliance forthwith.
